subject: Telemetry-driven pool sizing and tiered burst pricing for Origo Health
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@origohealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing ask + telemetry (attached)

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the call last week. We're getting closer to a committed model for our production rollout and need a concrete dedicated capacity proposal (GPU pool sizing + committed monthly price + burst/tier rules). Attaching two weeks of telemetry (aug 24 - sep 6) that shows our current production traffic. High-level:~120 sustained requests/sec, daily peak bursts to ~250 req/sec (short windows, 1-2 minutes), avg response payload ~350 tokens, max context length we use ~6k tokens for some clinical note completions (rare, ~5% of traffic).

Important asks from Origo procurement:
- SLA: target 99th latency <= 350ms for chat completions
- We want a 12-month reserved commit with the ability to burst beyond commit for short windows without extra engineering work
- Target commercial ask: baseline discount vs list for a 12-month commit, and a second-tier discount for a 24-month/expanded commit if we increase commit after 3 months

Can you and your team size the pool and propose a pricing/discount path (commit monthly $ / equivalent GPUs) and how burst capacity would be handled? Also call out whether KV/prefix caching or request batching could meaningfully reduce the pool size (we can instrument).

I've cc'd infra@origohealth.com for any raw telemetry Qs.

Attachments: origo_telemetry_aug-sep.csv, initial_commit_request.xlsx

Thanks,
Emma Liu
CTO, Origo Health
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing ask + telemetry (attached)

Hi Emma — thanks for the data. We'll review telemetry and get back with a recommended pool + commit structure. Two quick clarifying Qs that will materially change sizing: 

1) Is the 350 tokens figure average total tokens generated per request (post-prompt), or does that include prompt tokens too?
2) For the 6k context cases, are those full-turn requests (single long completion) or multi-turn chat where earlier turns can be cached?

We can usually size for sustained baseline + a burst policy that grants short-term autoscale credits (e.g., guaranteed baseline plus burst pool that spins up within 30s). I'll schedule an internal sizing sync but also happy to do a 30-min call with your infra folks if helpful.

Logan
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Logan — thanks. Quick answers:
- 350 tokens = avg total output tokens per request (we include prompt + completion in our telemetry export; prompt avg ~110 tokens, completion ~240 tokens).
- 6k contexts are mostly single-turn document-completion jobs (rare), ~90% of traffic is multi-turn chat with context reuse. We can enable prefix/KV caching for chat reuse for most users.

If you want finer-grain telemetry, infra@origohealth.com can share per-endpoint histograms. We're aiming to commit in the next 10 business days, so a pricing sketch this week would be ideal.

—Emma
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Marissa/Ben — forwarding Origo's telemetry and the ask (attached again). Key constraints: 120 RPS sustained, 250 RPS short peaks, avg prompt+completion ~350 tokens, rare 6k-context single-turn jobs (~5%). They want a 12-month reserved commit with burst capability and an upfront discount ask (baseline + expansion path).

Can you please:

Please enumerate options (baseline commit pool, burst headroom) and whether caching can materially reduce baseline.
- Ben: suggest the commercial framework: monthly committed $ amount per tier, baseline discount vs list, and a short-burst overage policy (credits / burst buckets). Also call out a two-tier path to 24 months if they expand commit after 3 months.

We need a sketched proposal by EOD Thursday (9/9).

Thanks — Logan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Origo Health telemetry — sizing + commercial ask

Team — I reviewed Origo's telemetry and ran quick capacity estimates. Summary (high level):

- Workload: 120 RPS steady => ~42k tokens/sec sustained (350 tokens * 120 RPS). Peak short bursts to 250 RPS => ~87.5k tokens/sec for ≤2 minutes.
- Model profile: 12B quantized inference (FP16/INT8 mix) — our internal benchmarks show ~8–9k tokens/sec per H100-equivalent when serving with optimized kernels for this model class at 16k context disabled; context length increases per-token cost linearly. For their mix (95% <=4k, 5% 6k single-turn), I'll conservatively estimate 8k tokens/sec per H100 equiv.

Sizing recommendation (3 options):
1) Conservative commit (recommended): 6 H100-equivalents baseline pool -> ~48k tokens/sec capacity (covers 120 RPS sustained with ~15% headroom). Add a burst policy that allows autoscale up to 9 H100-eq for short windows (handle 87.5k tokens/sec peak).
2) Lower-cost commit (risk-tolerant): 5 H100-eq baseline + burst to 8 H100-eq. This reduces monthly committed $ but increases reliance on autoscale; may cause slight 99th latency variability during very high peaks for 6k-context jobs.
3) Performance-first (higher commit): 8 H100-eq baseline to cover sustained + bursts without relying on fast autoscale.

Caching impact: enabling KV/prefix caching for multi-turn chat is estimated to reduce compute needs by ~18–25% for Origo's traffic pattern (they indicated 90% chat reuse). If Origo enables caching aggressively, the baseline could drop by ~1 H100-equivalent (so 5 -> 4 or 6 -> 5). We should present both cached and uncached numbers.

Operational notes:
- Autoscale burst policy: spin-up to additional H100-eq within ~30s; for 1–2 minute bursts we recommend a burst credit bucket (prepaid burst capacity) to avoid cold spin-up penalties.
- SLA: to meet 99th <=350ms we should recommend the conservative commit (option 1) or cached lower-cost plus higher burst credits.

I'll propose pricing inputs to Ben for numbers. Attaching a quick cost model: redwood_prelim_cost_model.xlsx

Marissa
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Origo Health telemetry — sizing + commercial ask

Logan/Marissa — pricing sketch below (ballpark for the EOD ask). Assumptions: 6 H100-eq baseline (option 1), 12-month commit, US region, list monthly price per H100-eq (hosting & infra + infra op premium) = $16,500/H100-eq.

Proposal A (Conservative, Option 1):
- Baseline: 6 H100-eq committed -> list $99,000/month
- 12-month reserved discount: 18% -> committed price $81,180/month
- Burst: prepaid burst credits sized for 200% of baseline for short windows (we suggest an initial 1000 burst-credit-minutes per month included). Overages billed at a discounted burst rate (40% off list).
- Expansion path: if Origo increases commit to >=8 H100-eq within first 90 days, an incremental 5% additional discount applied to the new capacity for remainder of term.

Proposal B (Cached, lower baseline):
- Baseline: 5 H100-eq committed -> list $82,500/month
- 12-month reserved discount: 15% -> committed price $70,125/month
- Same burst credit structure but recommend adding a small performance SLA credit pool to cover cold spin-ups for rare 6k-context jobs.

Commercial asks from Origo we should expect / negotiate:
- Origo likely to ask for 20%+ discount on 12-months. We can position 18% + a startup credit (1 month free or $50k onboarding credit) and avoid deeper list discount.
- Consider adding a commit accelerator: 2 months free if they sign a 24-month pure commit or 6% additional discount if they prepay quarterly.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Send both option A (6 H100-eq) and option B (5 H100-eq + caching) to Emma with clear expected 99th latency outcomes.
2) Offer a limited-time commercial incentive: 18% discount + $50k onboarding credit (one-time) if they sign within 10 business days.
3) Include a burst credit bucket and an operational runbook for cold spin-ups.

I'll draft the outbound note to Origo; Logan, want me to include numeric month-to-month payment schedule and a sample clause for burst credits?

Ben
Senior Account Exec — Redwood Inference
